label: 2026 Orbital Launches
delta: 97 Falcon-family launches in 2026 as of Aug 19: Starlink Group 17-50 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1097 12th flight, 24 V2-Mini satellites) launched at 04:01 UTC, widely reported as SpaceX's 100th mission of 2026 overall (a tally that also includes Starship integrated flight tests), pushing the Starlink constellation past roughly 11,000 satellites in orbit. Previously: the Aug 15 doubleheader — Globalstar 2-R (SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1090 14th flight) and the classified USSF-366 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1088 18th flight) launched just 38 minutes 31 seconds apart from opposite coasts, a new SpaceX record beating the prior 65-minute dual-launch mark (Aug 2024). Roughly 75% of 2026's missions have been Starlink. SpaceX passed its 90th Falcon 9 launch of the year on Aug 4 and its 50th launch from the West Coast in 2026 on Aug 8. President Gwynne Shotwell projects ~140-145 Falcon 9 launches for the full year (2024: 138 total missions; 2025: 167). Also in this window: Starship IFT-13 flew (test flight, not counted toward this Falcon-family total) — T-0 abort July 16, successful launch July 24; IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) remains pending Ship 41 static-fire testing at Starbase's Massey Outpost (Ship 41 arrived there Aug 19), with an FCC filing showing a NET Aug 28 target.

label: Total Booster Recoveries (All-Time)
delta: 651st: droneship 'Of Course I Still Love You' landing in the Pacific (its 219th touchdown) after the Aug 19 Starlink Group 17-50 mission from Vandenberg (B1097, 12th flight). 650th: OCISLY landing after the Aug 15 USSF-366 mission from Vandenberg (B1088, 18th flight) — the second half of a record 38.5-minute dual-launch turnaround. 649th (same day): Landing Zone 40 touchdown after the Aug 15 Globalstar 2-R mission from Cape Canaveral (B1090, 14th flight). 648th: ASOG landing after the Aug 11 Starlink 10-19 mission from Cape Canaveral (B1085, 18th flight). 647th: OCISLY landing during the Aug 8 Starlink West Coast mission (163rd touchdown on that droneship). 638th: ASOG landing (Starlink 10-45, July 14, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral — B1080 28th flight; SpaceX's 600th flight-proven-booster launch overall; ASOG's 161st touchdown). Note: IFT-12 Booster 19 (May 22) and IFT-13 Booster 20 (July 24) were NOT recovered — both lost during off-nominal landing-burn/splashdown attempts in Gulf of Mexico ocean landings (Starship boosters are not counted in this Falcon-family recovery tally).

label: Starlink Satellites in Orbit
delta: ~10,979 satellites in orbit (~10,963 operational, approaching 11,000) as of the Aug 19 Starlink Group 17-50 launch (24 V2-Mini sats from Vandenberg, B1097 12th flight). Previously: 10,898 in orbit (10,882 operational) as of early Aug 2026, out of 12,644 ever launched (per KeepTrack X-Report). SpaceX filed an FCC application July 6 for up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites across two new VLEO shells with W-/D-band frequencies, positioned as AI-data-center backhaul infrastructure in addition to consumer broadband. Aug 4 Q2 earnings: Starlink generated $4.3B of SpaceX's $7.81B quarterly revenue (55% of total).

label: Starlink Subscribers
delta: 12M subscribers per Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 4), up 66% YoY. Starlink revenue $4.3B in Q2 2026 (55% of SpaceX's total). Previously: 10.3M subscribers confirmed in the May 20, 2026 S-1 filing (doubled YoY); Starlink segment profit $1.2B in Q1 2026. 160+ countries served. ARPU: $66/month Q1 2026.

label: Max Single Booster Reflights
delta: B1067 set a new record with its 36th flight on the Starlink 10-42 mission (July 9, 2026, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral) — the first orbital booster in history to reach 36 flights. Previously: 34th flight on Starlink 10-44 (Mar 30, 2026).

label: Starship Integrated Flight Tests
delta: IFT-13 (Booster 20 V3 + Ship 40 V3) completed July 24, 2026 after a July 16 T-0 abort (6 Raptors flagged low LOX turbopump pressure from moisture; 2 engines replaced before reflight). Results: first-ever deployment of operational satellites — 20 V3 Starlink sats (6 with cameras) released in suborbit and contacted ground stations; Ship 40 relit all 3 Raptors and made a soft Indian Ocean splashdown, remaining intact afterward for the first close-up post-flight heat-shield inspection. Booster 20 was lost on its Gulf of Mexico splashdown attempt — only 10 of 13 landing-burn engines relit, 5 shut down seconds later, causing a hard impact. IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) update: Ship 41 departed to the Massey Outpost static-fire stand at Starbase on Aug 19 for single-engine static-fire testing; an FCC filing shows a NET Aug 28 target window (FAA-dependent), aiming for the first delivery of operational V3 Starlinks to full orbit and a possible first tower catch attempt of the upper stage. Prior: FAA cleared Starship to resume flights July 13, 2026, closing the IFT-12 mishap investigation (heat effects on propulsion + erroneous engine alarm settings that prevented Booster 19's reignition, May 22 loss).

label: SPCX (Nasdaq) — Post-IPO Trading
source: SEC EDGAR S-1 / CNBC / Bloomberg / Nasdaq / StockAnalysis.com
contestNote: Trading as low as $132.42 intraday Aug 20, 2026 (down ~5.2% from the prior close), extending a slide that began as a second major post-IPO lock-up tranche — about 319M restricted shares (~2.4% of shares outstanding, a potential ~20% float increase) — became eligible to trade. SPCX had closed Aug 19 at $139.65, down roughly 2.6-3%, as traders de-risked ahead of the unlock; the reaction diverges from the Aug 6 first-unlock experience, when 911.5M shares hit the float and the stock rose 6% that day and nearly 16% the next. The unlock coincided with confirmation that Starlink generated $4.3B in Q2 2026 revenue (55% of SpaceX's total) on 12M subscribers (+66% YoY), and that the Starlink constellation reached roughly 11,000 satellites in orbit. Bear-case analysts continue to flag traditional valuation models implying fair value as low as $10-30/share. Earlier: SPCX traded around $142/share intraday Aug 18 (day range $141.80-$143.00), down ~2.8-3.2% amid a broader growth-stock selloff (new US tariffs of 10-12.5% on imports from 60 countries, rising oil prices) and profit-taking ahead of the Aug 20 unlock — even after SpaceX announced a new Transporter rideshare launch contract for Vietnamese operator VinSpace's first satellites (targeted 2027). That followed a 4.45% rally to $146.23 on Aug 17 as mid-August 13F filings revealed SpaceX's largest institutional holders for the first time: Alphabet (~551.2M shares, ~$94B), Fidelity (~302.6M shares), Gigafund (~171.8M), Saudi PIF (~154.1M), Nvidia (~122.8M shares, ~$21B, via its xAI stake), and a first-time AMD position (~$565.5M); Harvard Management disclosed ~12.9M shares (~$2.2B) as its largest single U.S. equity holding. Earlier: SPCX fell 3.88% on Aug 14 — underperforming the 2.28%-down Telecommunications Services sector — as SpaceX's $60B all-stock closing of the Anysphere (Cursor) acquisition added ~391M new Class A shares to a market already digesting post-lockup supply. That interrupted a rally that had carried the stock from a 52-week low of $104.83 (Aug 3) to $146.15 intraday (Aug 13, +9.65% that day, driven by a filing showing Musk's 48.4% stake worth over $900B). Earlier in the window: Aug 6 lock-up expiration released up to 911.5M insider shares (~$100B) without triggering a sell-off (+6.1%); shares jumped 15.8% Aug 7-8 on the Q2 earnings beat and the $16.8B Terafab chip-plant confirmation; reclaimed the $135 IPO price Aug 10 (+4%); and surged 9.6% Aug 12 after Musk said AI/Grok revenue could overtake Starlink and launch revenue within 1-2 months. IPO recap: priced at $135/share June 11 (largest IPO in history, $1.77T implied valuation); all-time high $225.64 June 16; joined Nasdaq-100 July 7. Musk holds ~42-48% economic equity (filings vary by measurement date and post-Cursor dilution), ~79-85% voting control (dual-class Class B) — cannot be removed as director except by his own vote.
